HF Calling: Tradewind decodes HF selective calls (CCIR-493 style selcall, 100 baud FSK) and 2G ALE (8-FSK, MIL-STD-188-141) from the radio audio, answers calls to your IDs, and measures link quality so you know which channel and data mode to use. Needs the built-in sound modem and an SSB radio in USB.
Your own selcall IDs - 4 or 6 digits, up to 10, separated by commas. The first is the one you call from.
Your ALE addresses (letters and digits, up to 15). Blank uses your callsign, which is the amateur HFN practice.
Step through the channels, listening a moment on each, and stop when a call or ALE signal appears. Needs CAT control of the radio.
If the stations you call are scanning, the call needs a longer preamble so their scanner stops on your channel in time.
When someone sends you a beacon call, answer automatically with the 4-tone revertive and a signal report.
When someone ALE-calls one of your addresses, answer and complete the 3-way handshake automatically.
How long the dot pattern runs before a standard call. A scanning Barrett or Codan needs time to stop on your channel: 6 s is typical, up to 20 s for long scan lists.
If the radio you call is scanning, how many channels it scans. Tradewind then sends a preamble of 0.5 s per channel plus 1 s (Barrett's rule), so the scanner stops on your channel in time.
The standard selcall frame carries no callsign, so Tradewind sends your callsign in Morse after it (amateur identification).

Automatic uses the chat channels agreed for your zone. Manual override lets you type your own list, e.g. if a channel clashes with a local repeater or packet node. Channels on APRS, 145.010, weak-signal or satellite segments are refused.

Chats start on the APRS frequency, then move (QSY) to the first free channel here. Default: 144.510-144.590 (IARU Region 2 local-option segment - confirm with your national society) then 145.030-145.090 (data segment), 20 kHz apart because a 1200-baud FM signal is about 12 kHz wide. 145.010 is skipped: it is protected for Caribbean APRS.
The most packets the digipeater repeats in any minute (the 10%-of-airtime limit still applies).

Fill-in: only WIDE1-1 as the first hop, for areas that already have wide-area digipeaters. Wide-area: also WIDE2-1 and WIDE2-2 (never more than 2 hops) - for a high site serving a whole island that has no other digipeater.

Runs four 1200-baud decoders with different tone balance and clock tracking on the same audio, repairs packets with one or two bad bits, and decodes FX.25. In tests this gains about 1 dB, and about 2 dB with FX.25.

FM simplex frequency for Tradewind Robust FM, e.g. 145.570. Agree it with the other station and check it is free. Not 144.390 (APRS), 145.800-146.000 or 435-438 (satellites), and not a repeater input - Tradewind refuses the APRS and satellite frequencies.
USB dial frequency for Tradewind Robust and Robust DX. 2 m weak-signal segment, e.g. 144.150 - agree one with the stations on the other islands. HF: e.g. 10.142 (30 m) or 7.105 (40 m).
What the radio does on a pass: APRS beacons through the ISS, or receive (no transmitting): ISS SSTV pictures decoded by Tradewind, or BPSK telemetry decoded by gr-satellites.
While receiving, the radio is retuned every 10 s to follow the Doppler shift (about +-3.5 kHz on 2 m, +-10 kHz on 70 cm). Needs CAT (IC-9100, FT-991A...).
Keep the audio of each received pass in the RECEIVED list (about 6 MB a minute). Recordings that could not be decoded are always kept.

Satellite Watch Mode. Works out when the satellite passes over your grid square from its orbit (downloaded twice a day from CelesTrak and kept for offline use). A 6-character grid square gives the most accurate times.

Audio: 'USB Audio CODEC'. PTT port: the IC-705 USB serial port. On the radio set USB SEND to RTS, DATA MOD to USB, and use FM-D (data) mode. For automatic tuning, set PTT to 'Icom CI-V' with address A4 and tick 'Tune the radio'.

Audio: 'USB Audio CODEC'. PTT port: first IC-9700 USB serial port. Set USB SEND to RTS, DATA MOD to USB, use FM-D. For automatic tuning, set PTT to 'Icom CI-V' with address A2 and tick 'Tune the radio'.

One USB cable carries audio and CI-V. Audio: 'USB Audio CODEC'. PTT port: the IC-9100's USB serial port. On the radio set DATA MOD to USB, USB MOD Level about 25-50%, CI-V address 7C and CI-V baud 9600. With 'Tune the radio' on, Tradewind sets the frequency for you at power-on (2m on the main band): FM data for 1200 baud and Robust FM, USB data for Robust and Robust DX, and puts the radio back when you switch off. Close other CAT software (logger, WSJT-X) first - only one program can use the port.

The FT-2980R has no data jack or CAT port. Use a soundcard interface with a cable for Yaesu's 8-pin modular mic jack and the 3.5 mm external speaker jack: SignaLink USB (VOX), or a Digirig with Yaesu mic cable (set PTT to Serial RTS). Check the cable's mic-jack pinout against the radio manual. Set squelch just closed, keep TX audio low (mic audio is pre-emphasised), and use Low or Mid power for long sessions.
Use the 6-pin mini-DIN DATA jack with a SignaLink, Digirig or Easy Digi data cable. Set the radio's packet speed to 1200. PTT: VOX on a SignaLink, or Serial RTS on a Digirig.

These radios' built-in APRS has no KISS mode, so connect a soundcard interface to the rear DATA jack (cable for your model). Set the data jack speed to 1200 bps and turn the radio's own APRS off on that band. PTT: VOX or Serial RTS (Digirig).
Enable KISS mode on the radio, then choose its USB or Bluetooth serial port.
Put the built-in TNC in KISS mode (PACKET mode, then KISS ON). Use the COM port on the control head.

One USB cable. Audio: 'USB Audio CODEC'. PTT: the radio's USB COM port, Icom CI-V address 94. On the radio set CI-V USB Baud Rate to 19200 (or Auto), DATA MOD to USB, and use USB-D mode. HF packet uses the 300-baud modem (e.g. 10.1476 MHz USB for HF APRS).
Audio: 'USB Audio CODEC'. PTT: Icom CI-V address 98 on the USB COM port. Set DATA MOD to USB and use USB-D. 300-baud HF modem.

Use the 6-pin mini-DIN DATA jack with a SignaLink (VOX) or Digirig (Serial RTS) data cable. Set the data band and 1200 bps in the radio menu.
